900100.title: The Sketchbook Habit
900100.description: The design begins on paper: the jeweler's sketchbook discipline. The sketchbook habit is the designer's first tool: the daily drawing that trains the hand and the eye. The discipline is the volume — the sketchbook fills, and the filling is the learning. The technique is the iteration — the same ring drawn twenty ways, the twentieth better than the first. The habit's reward is the fluency: the hand that draws daily designs effortlessly. The sketchbook is the bench's memory; the habit is the designer's education.

900101.title: The Lost-Wax Casting
900101.description: The ancient magic: casting jewelry from wax. The lost-wax casting is the ancient magic: the wax model, the investment mold, the molten metal, the revealed form. The process is the transformation — the wax lost, the metal found. The craft is the wax working: the carving, the building, the detail at the scale of the finger. The casting's discipline is the sprue and the vent — the metal must flow and the air must flee. The lost-wax lesson is the patience: the mold waits, the metal pours, the form emerges. The wax is the dream; the metal is the memory.

900102.title: The Stone Setting Bench
900102.description: The meeting of metal and gem: the setting craft. The stone setting bench is where metal meets gem: the seat cut, the stone placed, the metal pushed over the girdle. The craft's families are the prong, the bezel, the pavé — each a different promise of security and light. The discipline is the seat: the bearing cut true, and the stone sits without rocking. The setting's test is the tap — the set stone rings solid, never rattles. The bench's lesson is the respect: the stone is the guest, the metal is the host. The seat is true; the stone is safe.

900103.title: The Engraving Burin
900103.description: The line cut in metal: the engraver's art. The engraving burin cuts the line in metal: the graver pushed, the curl rising, the design emerging in bright cut. The art's discipline is the control — the burin goes where the hand decides, at the depth the eye demands. The techniques are the lines: the bright cut, the wriggle, the stipple — each a different light. The engraving's patience is the practice plate: the thousand lines before the first commission. The burin's lesson is the commitment: the cut is forever, so the hand must be sure. The line is cut; the light is caught.

900104.title: The Mokume-Gane Layers
900104.description: Wood grain in metal: the layered art. The mokume-gane layers fuse the metals into wood grain: the stacked sheets, the bonded billet, the carved pattern revealing the strata. The art's origin is the Japanese sword furniture — the technique of the samurai's fittings, reborn in jewelry. The craft is the bond: the metals fused without solder, by heat and pressure alone. The pattern's reveal is the carving — the twisted billet cut to expose the grain. The mokume lesson is the patience: the billet cooks for hours, and the hurried bond fails. The layers are the story; the grain is the telling.
900104.signature_version: Signature version — this record is a Signature version in the Signature system.

900105.title: The Enamel Kiln
900105.description: Glass fused to metal: the enamel fire. The enamel kiln fuses glass to metal: the powdered glass, the painted design, the firing that melts it to jewel. The crafts are the champlevé, the cloisonné, the plique-à-jour — each a different conversation between metal and glass. The discipline is the firing: the kiln's heat, the watchful eye, the seconds that decide. The enamel's risk is the crack — the glass and metal expand differently, and the piece must survive the cooling. The kiln's lesson is the surrender: the fire decides, and the artist proposes. The glass melts; the color sings.

900106.title: The Filigree Wire
900106.description: Lace in metal: the filigree craft. The filigree wire twists metal into lace: the fine wires, the curled shapes, the soldered whole. The craft's delicacy is the wire — the hair-fine gold, twisted and shaped by tweezers. The technique is the frame: the outline first, the fill after, the solder in whispers. The filigree's patience is the piece count: the hundred wires, each placed. The lace's lesson is the lightness: the metal becomes air. The wire is the thread; the piece is the lace.
900106.signature_version: Signature version — this record is a Signature version in the Signature system.

demo.title: Interactive record tour - The Filigree Wire

900107.title: The Clasp Engineering
900107.description: The small machine: designing clasps that last. The clasp engineering designs the small machine: the box clasp, the toggle, the hidden catch — the mechanism the piece depends on. The engineering's criteria are the security (it must not open unbidden), the ease (it must open when asked), and the beauty (it must not show). The discipline is the wear: the clasp is tested for the thousand openings. The clasp's lesson is the humility: the smallest part carries the greatest responsibility. The machine is small; the trust is total.

900108.title: The Patina Chemistry
900108.description: Color from chemistry: the patina craft. The patina chemistry colors metal with chemistry: the liver of sulfur, the ammonia fume, the heat blush — each a controlled corrosion. The craft's control is the recipe: the concentration, the time, the temperature, each deciding the hue. The discipline is the test piece: the patina is proven on scrap before the piece. The patina's seal is the wax — the color locked under the protective coat. The chemistry's lesson is the intention: the tarnish, directed, becomes the art. The corrosion is controlled; the color is chosen.
